gisborne-6.name: Puhi Kai Iti / Cook Landing Site
gisborne-6.bio: The national historic reserve in Gisborne where Cook's crew landed in 1769, with a 1906 Cook Monument.
notes: Url is DOC's Gisborne area page (no separate reserve page). 24-hour access and visit time are assumptions.

gisborne-7.name: Eastwoodhill Arboretum
gisborne-7.bio: A national arboretum 35 km north-west of Gisborne with 25,000 species of trees and 25 km of trails.
notes: Adult entry NZD 18; closed Christmas Day; visit time is an estimate.

gisborne-8.name: Rere Rock Slide
gisborne-8.bio: A natural 60 m rock slide on the Wharekopae River, ridden on boogie boards or tyres, free and open all year.
notes: No ticketUrl: free public reserve, no single steward.
Safety wording not sourced and omitted. Rere Falls are a separate stop about 2 km east.

gisborne-9.name: Mōrere Springs Scenic Reserve
gisborne-9.bio: Salt-water hot springs piped to pools in a 364 ha reserve of rainforest and nikau palms, with free walks.
notes: Cost is the adult pool entry (NZD 20); the reserve walks are free. Hours Thu–Mon, closed Tue and Wed; DOC says check Facebook for changes.

gisborne-11.name: Waikanae Beach
gisborne-11.bio: A beach in the middle of town, a 10 to 15 minute walk from the centre, running on into Midway Beach.
notes: No ticketUrl: public beach. 24-hour access and visit time are assumptions. Held for a non-Commons photo.

east-cape-6.name: Anaura Bay
east-cape-6.bio: A bay where Cook's crew filled casks in 1769, with a beach campsite and a walkway to panoramic views.
notes: Beach is free; camping fees (DOC campsite and the motor camp) not checked, so not in the bio.

te-urewera-4.name: Lake Waikaremoana Great Walk
te-urewera-4.bio: A 46 km, three to four day tramp between Onepoto and Hopuruahine, with huts and campsites booked in advance.
notes: Cost NZD 57–105 is three nights adult camping (19 each) to three nights in huts (35 each); day walkers and entry to Te Urewera are free.
Coordinates are Hopuruahine Landing (northern end); the Onepoto shelter was not pinned.
DOC says huts are being removed in Te Urewera; Wikipedia says 44 km, DOC 46 km (DOC used).

whirinaki-conservation-park.name: Whirinaki Te Pua-a-Tāne Conservation Park
whirinaki-conservation-park.bio: A forest park south-east of Rotorua with tracks, huts and campsites, most walks starting from River Road.
notes: Entry free; hut and camp fees not checked. Visit time is an estimate. No waterfall track named by DOC, so none in the bio.

wairoa.name: Wairoa
wairoa.bio: The northernmost town in Hawke's Bay, with a museum and the old Portland Island lighthouse on Marine Parade.
notes: No ticketUrl. Hours and visit time generic. Gateway town; could be sent to review (no headline attraction).

mahia-peninsula.name: Māhia Peninsula
mahia-peninsula.bio: A peninsula of surf, diving and fishing, with a shallow family beach and a 374 ha lowland forest reserve.
notes: No ticketUrl. Portland Island lighthouse deliberately left out (private farmed land). Coordinates are Māhia Beach.

gisborne-1.bio: A reserve on a former pā above the city, with lookouts over the bay, walking tracks and a Cook monument.

gisborne-2.bio: A 600 m heritage wharf, the second longest in New Zealand, restored and reopened in 2013.
gisborne-2.notes: No wiki: it is a section of Tolaga Bay; remove any wiki field.

gisborne-5.hours: 10:00 AM – 4:00 PM (Sunday and public holidays 1:30 PM – 4:00 PM)
gisborne-5.notes: No wiki. Hours: Mon–Sat 10–4, Sun and public holidays 1:30–4; closed Good Friday, Christmas Day, Boxing Day (research). Remove free:true.

notes: gisborne-10 Young Nick's Head: held, reason 'access restricted: recommend review' (tourism guide says private farmland; Wikipedia says summit/cliffs are public reserve; no visit point found; old 'monument' claim unsourced). No bio written.
Photos: gisborne-11 Waikanae Beach still held for a non-Commons photo; held ids otherwise applied once a photo is found.
